# Chakkanipāta (AN 6)

**ID:** AN 6
**Section:** Aṅguttaranikāya (an)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Chakkanipāta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Book of the Sixes
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/an6

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Chakkanipāta* ("The Book of the Sixes") constitutes the sixth major division of the *Aṅguttaranikāya*, assembling discourses organized around doctrinal groupings of six items [SuttaCentral]. Several of its discourses are central to Buddhist doctrine and meditation practice. AN 6.63 (*Nibbedhikasutta*) is well known for the Buddha's quintessential definition of action (*kamma*) as intention (*cetanāhaṁ, bhikkhave, kammaṁ vadāmi; cetayitvā kammaṁ karoti kāyena vācāya manasā*) [IABU 2012; Walshe 1987]. In AN 6.55 (*Soṇasutta*), the Buddha instructs the monk Soṇa to balance effort like the tuned strings of a lute and to grasp the theme or sign (*nimitta*) without restlessness or laxity [Polak 2011]. AN 6.46 (*Mahācunda Sutta*) addresses an ancient debate or tension between meditators (*jhāyins*) and doctrine-oriented practitioners (*dhammayogins*) [Polak 2011]. Other notable suttas include AN 6.16, featuring Nakulamātā comforting her dying husband [Anālayo 2016]; AN 6.56 (*Phaggunasutta*), on the sick monk Phagguna's eradication of the five lower fetters and the six benefits of timely reflection on the Dhamma [Anālayo 2016]; AN 6.29, on sustaining mindfulness through the postures [Wen]; AN 6.68, on right view as an indispensable prerequisite for right concentration [Wen]; and AN 6.99–100, treating the contemplation of suffering and non-self, which are also cited in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Wen].

Cross-canonical parallels for the *Chakkanipāta* are abundant: SuttaCentral records parallels across Northern Āgama collections, including eleven in the *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ), ten in the *Madhyamāgama* (MĀ), seven in the *Ekottarikāgama* (EĀ), two in the second *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ²), and three individual Taishō translations [SuttaCentral]. Specific parallels include AN 6.52 (*Khattiyasutta*) matching MĀ 149 and EĀ 37.8 [SuttaCentral; Kieschnick], AN 6.55 corresponding to MĀ 123, SĀ 254, and EĀ 23.3 [SuttaCentral], and AN 6.56 matching SĀ 1023 [SuttaCentral; Anālayo 2016]. Machine text-reuse detection by DharmaNexus corroborates extensive alignments with Chinese translations of the *Madhyamāgama* (T 26), *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99), and T 57, as well as Sanskrit texts (*Daśabalasūtra*, *Lalitavistara*, *Saṅghabhedavastu*) and Tibetan translations (*Abhidharmakośaṭīkopāyikā*, D4094; *Vinayavastu*, D1) [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus indicates heavy formulaic and textual sharing with neighboring divisions of the Aṅguttaranikāya (particularly AN 5, AN 10, AN 8, and AN 4), DN 33 (*Saṅgīti Sutta*), and various chapters of the Saṁyuttanikāya (SN 35, SN 22, SN 12, SN 46, and SN 47) [DharmaNexus].
